cards.front: What two kinds of member can a class body contain?
cards.extra: Variables declared in a class are instance variables; methods define what the object can do. A class may have any number of either.
cards.source: Keep On Coding — Java Classes & Objects (https://youtu.be/IUqKuGNasdM?t=86)
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::01 Classes and Objects

cards.back: A variable declared in the class body, of which each object gets its own copy
cards.extra: Two objects of the same class can hold different values for their fields — that is what makes them distinct instances.
cards.source: Keep On Coding — Java Classes & Objects (https://youtu.be/IUqKuGNasdM?t=86)
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::01 Classes and Objects

cards.front: How do you declare and create an object?
cards.extra: new allocates the object in memory, then the reference is assigned to the variable. Assignment is right-to-left: the object exists before the name points at it.
cards.source: Keep On Coding — Java Classes & Objects (https://youtu.be/IUqKuGNasdM?t=189)
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::01 Classes and Objects

cards.front: What does the dot operator do on an object?
cards.back: Reaches into the object to access its fields and methods — p1.name, p1.attack()
cards.extra: Every member access goes through the dot; it is how you tell one object's state from another's.
cards.source: Keep On Coding — Java Classes & Objects (https://youtu.be/IUqKuGNasdM?t=243)
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::01 Classes and Objects

cards.front: If you change one object's field, what happens to another object of the same class?
cards.back: Nothing — each object has its own copy of the instance variables
cards.extra: This isolation is the point of objects: state and behaviour are encapsulated per instance.
cards.source: Keep On Coding — Java Classes & Objects (https://youtu.be/IUqKuGNasdM?t=317)
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::01 Classes and Objects

cards.front: What three rules identify a constructor?
cards.back: Same name as the class, no return type — not even void — and it runs automatically when the object is created
cards.extra: A method with a return type is not a constructor, even with the right name — the missing return type is what distinguishes it, and it is the reason a constructor is never inherited.
cards.source: Keep On Coding — Java Classes & Objects (https://youtu.be/IUqKuGNasdM?t=370)
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::01 Classes and Objects

cards.front: What value does an int instance field hold before any assignment?
cards.extra: Locals do not: an unassigned local is a compile error. A constructor that sets the field overrides the default.
cards.source: Keep On Coding — Java Classes & Objects (https://youtu.be/IUqKuGNasdM?t=430)
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::01 Classes and Objects

cards.front: How do you pass values into an object at creation?
cards.back: Through the constructor's parameters, supplied in the parentheses after new
cards.extra: new Pokemon("Eevee", 25) — the arguments arrive as parameters and are typically assigned to the fields.
cards.source: Keep On Coding — Java Classes & Objects (https://youtu.be/IUqKuGNasdM?t=442)
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::01 Classes and Objects

cards.front: What happens if a constructor parameter has the same name as a field?
cards.back: The parameter wins — name = name assigns the parameter to itself and the field is never set
cards.extra: Java resolves a bare name to the most local declaration. The assignment compiles, does nothing, and leaves the field at its default.
cards.source: Keep On Coding — Java Classes & Objects (https://youtu.be/IUqKuGNasdM?t=553)
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::01 Classes and Objects

cards.front: How do you make a name refer to the field rather than a parameter of the same name?
cards.extra: this means "the object this code is running in", so this.name is unambiguously the field.
cards.source: Keep On Coding — Java Classes & Objects (https://youtu.be/IUqKuGNasdM?t=593)
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::01 Classes and Objects

cards.front: Why should a class represent a single cohesive entity?
cards.back: Because mixing unrelated data — an age and the weather in a Person class — makes the code messy and the model meaningless
cards.extra: A class that holds only what belongs to one concept is easier to name, reuse and test.
cards.source: Keep On Coding — Java Classes & Objects (https://youtu.be/IUqKuGNasdM?t=115)
